newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA says proposal could save C$500 mln.
newsitem.headline: NOVA says proposal could save C$500 mln.

text.p: NOVA Corp's proposal to have its pipeline network act as the Canadian portion of the producer-backed Alliance pipeline could save C$500 million in industry expenditures on Alberta gas pipelines, said Bruce Simpson, president of NOVA unit NOVA Gas Transmission.

Simpson said Alliance's Canadian portion would likely cost C$1 billion to construct, and NOVA could build the necessary facilities for C$400 million -- assuming all of the gas was incremental, or not currently moving on its own system.
"Even if you made that assumption, we'd still (spend) half a billion dollars less capital than what's being proposed," he said in a telephone interview.
But Simpson said it was more likely that volumes that would move on Alliance would be taken from NOVA's system, duplicating pipelines and stranding NOVA facilities.
"As we analyze the (Alliance) project, the volumes are basically displacement off of our system onto the Alliance Pipeline," he said.
Alliance confirmed earlier it was devising a response to NOVA's proposal to combine the two systems. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
